proposal:
VERDICT: no credible universal mechanism and no polynomial SAT algorithm. Everything below is hand-derived, unexecuted and not machine-checked. One EXPERIMENT outside scc-emra-ialh5-v1: TON, translation-orbit normalisation, run at root and at every node after Canon. It replaces BLQ's rewriting with the action of the flip group F_2^n on clause sets.

REPRESENTATION. tau_t flips the literals of the variables in t. For each exact support S (all widths; narrower clauses are their own blocks), Z_S is the set of falsifying points, W_S its stabiliser and A_S the annihilator of W_S. W(F) = {t : t|S in W_S for all S} = {t : tau_t(F)=F}. All data are bit-vectors of length n.

(1) PINNING. Take a reduced echelon basis of W(F) with pivot set P. Add units x_p=0 for p in P, re-Canon, and repeat to a fixpoint. Soundness S4: if m models F and w is in W, then m+w models F; choosing w as the sum of basis vectors b_p with m_p=1 clears P. So F and F+units are equisatisfiable, and any model of the pinned formula is a model of F. There is no rewriting, no compatible basis, and the clause count never increases. Dependent forms (last round's U6 triangle) need no special case.

(2) ORBIT KEY. F ~ F' iff tau_t(F)=F' for some t. T_S = {u : Z_S+u = Z'_S} is empty or a coset of W_S, so the test is one GF(2) system. Canonical representative: visit supports in lexicographic order, keeping an affine set U of admissible t. For block S, compute m = the minimum over z in Z_S of the least element of z+U|S (echelon reduction). The candidates are u=z+m lying in U|S, at most |Z_S| of them. Keep those whose sorted image is lex-least; they form a coset of W_S, which is intersected with U. Output tau_t(F) for any t in the final U. This is used only as a dedup hash key after the exact prune; the stored state is unchanged. Soundness S5: orbit-equal states are equisatisfiable and models transfer by t.

WORK per node, with N the encoded length: stabilisers and candidates cost O(sum |Z_S|^2 |S|) <= O(N^2) bit operations, and odd |Z_S| gives W_S=0 at once. There are at most N equations, so elimination costs O(n^2 N). No integers appear. TOTAL work = (number of states) x poly(N), and the number of states is unbounded (U4).

HAND CONSEQUENCES.
T3: if F is the direct encoding of G composed with ANY affine forms, plus XOR constraints, pinning leaves n - dim W(F) variables.
T4: for direct-encoded Tseitin on any graph of any degree, W is the cycle space, the non-pivots form a spanning forest, leaves become units, and UP refutes at root. This is width-free and polynomial in the 2^(d-1)-clause input.

PREDICTIONS for the experiment (not the deployed target):
P1, supplied auto00007: dim W=8, P={1,2,4,5,7,8,10,11}. Canon leaves (-3|6),(-6|9),(-9|-3),(3|12),(-12|6),(-9|-12). Literals 3 and -3 share an SCC, so root UNSAT with zero branches (deployed peak 16).
P2, auto00005: dim W=9. The three surviving variables form a spanning tree of K4 and UP refutes at root with k=5 unchanged.
P3, auto00006, if the lift is XOR of disjoint pairs: dim W=6, a 9-clause 2-CNF, root UNSAT.
P4, control: adding clause (1 2 3 4 5 7) to auto00007 drops dim W to 3 (t8=t9, block 10-12 even).
missing_theorem:
M0: S4, S5, T3, T4 and the canonical-key correctness are hand arguments only.

FIRST UNSUPPORTED THEOREM, U9 (monotonicity): under the same order, peak_TON(F) <= peak_current(F).

ATTEMPTED REFUTATION. The natural proof is a simulation in which every TON state is a translate of a deployed state. It breaks in two places.
(a) Prune-stronger is not orbit-compatible. The deployed run may hold G and its translate G0 and drop G'_1..G'_m as supersets of G. TON merges G into G0; no G'_i contains G0, so all m survive, giving 1+m states against 2. I have not constructed an explicit formula, but the simulation argument is dead. The obvious repair is orbit-pruning (drop G' if it contains some translate of G). That repair is REFUTED as a polynomial step: with single-clause blocks in G, T_S = Z'_S + z is an arbitrary set, so deciding whether t exists is a general CSP (1-in-3 SAT embeds) and is NP-complete.
(b) Pinning units change occurrence products, and hence the DP order and the <= acceptance.
So U9 is unproved and I expect it to be false in corner cases.

U9' (repaired, still unproved): with pinning off and prune-stronger off in both runs, and no IALH truncation, TON's layer size equals the number of translation orbits of the deployed layer. This needs equivariance lemma E: Canon, SCC representative choice, DP order and acceptance, and IALH all commute with tau_t. E fails if any tie-break reads literal sign or if the 128-row cap selects rows in a polarity-dependent way. Soundness does not depend on E.

U10: semantic lineality (models closed under w although tau_w(F) != F) is coNP-hard to detect. TON sees only the syntactic W.

U4 (growth gap, unchanged): there is no polynomial state bound. For PHP, random 3-CNF, or any formula where each variable lies in a block with odd |Z_S|, W=0 and orbits are trivial, so TON is a no-op costing O(N^2) per node.
self_attack:
1. Narrow. W != 0 needs every block touching a moving variable to have even |Z_S| and a shared stabiliser. One singleton-support clause freezes its whole support (P4). An adversary pays one clause per block to disable TON, and I have no robust variant (U8 stays open).
2. Encoding escape. XORs split by auxiliary variables keep W, because the auxiliaries move with it. Lifting through AND, OR or majority gadgets gives W=0. That case falls back to the earlier OTPQ idea, which is unverified.
3. T3 only moves the adversary to the base formula G. The residual-state count on G is untouched. This is restricted-family detection, not completeness.
4. T4 is known mathematics: Gaussian elimination solves Tseitin. Its only content here is that it falls out of a width-free symmetry computation with no parity recognition. An inconsistent XOR system with an injective matrix has W=0 and may yield no units; then only IALH at k=5 remains.
5. Overhead. TON costs O(N^2) per node where it never fires, on top of the measured ~22x IALH overhead on auto00006. The skip test (stop once every variable is frozen by some block) is unmeasured.
6. Canonical key. The argument that ties form a coset assumes images are compared as sorted sets. An implementation comparing in input order would be wrong and could merge inequivalent states only if the final verification tau_t(F)=key is omitted, so that check is mandatory.
7. Orbit dedup may fire rarely once pinning is on, since sibling equivalences induced by global symmetries are already removed. Its marginal value is an open empirical question.
mechanism_signature: TON: translation-orbit normalisation at every node. Flip group F_2^n acting on clause sets; per-support stabilisers by |Z_S|^2 hashing; W(F) by GF(2) elimination; pivot pinning x_p=0 as complete symmetry breaking for W; polynomial canonical orbit key by lex-greedy affine refinement, used as a residual dedup key. Width-free, no rewriting, no compatible basis. Experiment outside scc-emra-ialh5-v1.
delta_from_prior:
Last round's BLQ was root-only, rewrote F into quotient variables, needed a compatible basis (resting on an unverified distributive-lattice fact) and returned SKIP on dependent forms (U6).
New this round:
(1) Pinning replaces rewriting. It needs no basis, removes the distributivity dependence, and gains exactly dim W on dependent forms.
(2) It runs per node, so lineality that appears after branching is used.
(3) A polynomial canonical key for residuals modulo polarity flips. This is the first concrete tractable fragment of the unimplemented isomorphism/twin quotient; variable identity stays fixed, so it is not graph isomorphism.
(4) T4: width-free Tseitin refutation by pinning plus UP.
(5) A negative result: orbit-pruning is NP-complete.
(6) U9 attacked; the simulation proof fails at prune-stronger and at DP order.
(7) Predictions P1-P4, with P1 worked by hand on the supplied 96-clause formula.
Unchanged: U4, and no universality claim.
